ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: An export processing zone refers to a special area established by a country or region to utilize foreign capital, mainly for manufacturing, processing, or assembling export commodities. Enterprises settling there can enjoy many preferential treatments such as rapid customs clearance, bonded tax exemption, and tax rebates without leaving the processing zone. The following figure is a “schematic map of the distribution of China's export processing zones.” <image1> What is the leading factor attracting foreign-funded enterprises to settle in export processing zones?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An export processing zone refers to a special area established by a country or region to utilize foreign capital, mainly for manufacturing, processing, or assembling export commodities. Enterprises settling there can enjoy many preferential treatments such as rapid customs clearance, bonded tax exemption, and tax rebates without leaving the processing zone. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a schematic map of the distribution of China’s export processing zones: on the map of China, black dots mark the locations of export processing zones; the black dots are mainly concentrated in the eastern coastal areas, with a small number also distributed in inland areas. Returning to the text of the question, export processing zones are special areas established by a country or region to utilize foreign investment, and enterprises entering the zones can enjoy preferential treatments such as fast customs clearance, bonded tax exemption, and tax rebates. These conditions belong to institutional arrangements and preferential measures provided by the government, so the leading factor attracting foreign-funded enterprises to settle in export processing zones is policy.
